text: In `public static void main(String[] args)`, what does `static` actually buy you?
choices: It lets the JVM call the method without constructing an object first, which matters because at startup no object of your class exists yet.
It makes the method run before any other code, which is why it is the entry point.
It allocates the method in a fixed memory region so the JVM can locate it by address.
It prevents the method from being overridden, guaranteeing the program starts in your class.
explanation: The launcher has a class name and nothing else. A non-static method would need a receiver, so the JVM would have to construct one — which would require choosing a constructor and having something to pass it. `static` sidesteps the regress. Chapter 19 gives the full account, and the point of raising it now is that every word in that signature is a decision with a reason rather than an incantation.
